example_flows.t: Lipstick: one studio shot becomes a vanity scene and a shade swatch
example_flows.d: The starting photo was a single coral lipstick on a plain studio background. From it we made a scene on a marble vanity beside a mirror and a fresh flower, and a close-up next to a swatch of the same shade, so shoppers can judge the color before they buy.

example_flows.t: Hoodie: a flat product photo becomes street style and a flat lay
example_flows.d: We started with a front view of a plain gray hoodie. From it we made an image of someone wearing it on an autumn street and a flat lay on a wooden bench with a beanie and a scarf, so the same item works on a product page and in social posts.

example_flows.t: Coffee beans: a plain bag in a kitchen and at a breakfast table
example_flows.d: We started with a photo of a kraft coffee bag with a blank label and a scatter of beans. From it we made a kitchen counter scene with a pour-over brewer and a mug, and a breakfast table with a croissant, so the product looks at home in the moments people drink it.

ugc.title: What is an AI UGC video ad?
paras: UGC stands for user-generated content. A UGC-style ad looks like a short clip a customer filmed on their phone: casual, close to the product and made for TikTok, Reels and Shorts rather than TV.

An [AI UGC video ad](page:video-ads) gives you that look without hiring a creator or shipping your product to anyone. You upload a photo of your product, pick a style or describe the scene, and AIVideosUGC makes a 6, 10, 15 or 30 second clip built around your real product.

The people in these clips are generated by AI, not real customers, so use them to show the product rather than as reviews. Captions, music and prices go on afterward in your editor or ad tool, where you control every word.

faq.q: What can I make with AIVideosUGC?
faq.a: Short video ads, product and unboxing videos, white-background photos, lifestyle photos, model photos and social ad images. Most start from a photo of your product.
A clear photo of the product you sell. A phone photo on a plain background works well. Only upload photos you own or have permission to use.

faq.q: How long are the videos, and what sizes can I get?
faq.a: Videos are 6, 10, 15 or 30 seconds. Choose 9:16 for TikTok, Reels and Shorts, 1:1 for feeds, or 16:9 for wider placements.

faq.q: How many videos and photos do I get each month?
faq.a: A product photo or a 6-second video uses 24 credits, a 10-second video 40, a 15-second video 60 and a 30-second video 120. The Starter plan's 200 credits cover about eight photos or three 15-second videos a month.

faq.q: Is the person in the video a real creator?
faq.a: No. The people in AI UGC videos are generated by AI, so show the product with them rather than presenting the clip as a customer review. Some platforms ask you to label AI-generated content.

faq.q: Does it add spoken narration or music?
faq.a: No. Add captions and music in TikTok or CapCut after you download, and type prices or offers in your editor or ad tool so every word is exactly right.

faq.q: Can I try it for free?
faq.a: Not right now. There's no free plan, and checkout isn't open yet — the pricing page lists the planned Starter, Pro and Premium offers. Every photo or video shows its credit cost before it's made.

faq.q: Can I use the images and videos I make commercially?
faq.a: Yes. You can use the images and videos you make in your own ads, product pages and social posts.

faq.q: Do downloaded images and videos have an AIVideosUGC watermark?
faq.a: No. Downloaded images and videos do not include an AIVideosUGC watermark.

overview.h2: Choose the first asset your product needs
overview.d: Start with the decision in front of you. A new listing usually needs a clean product view; a product already on sale may need a social image or a short video opening. One upload can lead to several tests, so you can build a small set around the same item instead of planning a new shoot for every placement.

overview.h2: Use the output for its job
overview.d: Keep a white-background image for the main product view, use a lifestyle frame to show context, and reserve a short video for movement or an unboxing moment. The result is generated from your product photo, while your final price, date, offer, music, and captions stay under your control in the editor or ad tool.

input_guide.h2: Prepare one photo that can carry the details

items.d: For bottles, boxes, and electronics, show the entire outline and keep labels facing the camera so the shape is easy to preserve.
Lay clothing, bedding, or bags flat or on a hanger with straps and openings visible; a hidden corner gives later scenes less to work with.
Include the whole piece and a useful scale cue for jewelry, glasses, or a watch, then choose a close-up or worn scene that matches that scale.
Use a clean angle for metal, glass, and glossy packaging; strong glare can make a color or printed mark harder to carry into a new scene.

results.h2: Know what each choice costs and returns

items.d: An image generation uses 24 credits and returns a square asset for a listing, collection grid, or feed post.
A 6, 10, 15, or 30 second video uses 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits. The exact cost appears before the job starts.
Pick 9:16 for vertical short-form placements, 1:1 for a feed, or 16:9 for a wide placement; 4:3 and 3:4 are also available when a destination calls for them.
Your upload and the finished file stay inside your account, ready for you to download and place in your store or ad process.

scene_recipes.h2: Six starting recipes for one product

items.d: Place the shoe on a damp trail beside a small puddle, with the side profile facing the camera and open sky above for later ad copy.
Show the mug beside an open book on a breakfast table, with the handle turned toward the viewer and morning light from one side.
Open the charging case on a tidy desk beside a laptop, with both earbuds visible and no extra device competing for attention.
Set the tube on a bright bathroom shelf beside a folded towel, keeping the front label facing forward and the background quiet.
Show the bag on a city doorway hook with the handles clear, then make a second frame with the same bag carried at a weekend market.
Place the bottle beside tacos on a wooden table, leaving one open side for a headline that you will add after download.
Type the price, date, discount code, and product claims in your design or ad tool instead of relying on lettering inside the generated image.
For a video, choose the music, captions, and any voice treatment in the destination editor where you can check timing and spelling.
Compare the file with the real item before it goes live, especially the label, color, count, and small hardware details.
